extracted.intended_audience: researchers, librarians, publishers, and readers interested in research integrity and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: News coverage and documentation of a publisher retracting an academic/technical book because of integrity problems (fake references, undeclared AI use), and the publisher's retraction process and responses. Focus is on explaining what went wrong, publisher actions, and community reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, trustworthiness, and editorial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature said it is 'committed to publishing content that is accurate, trustworthy, and aligned with the highest editorial standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher expectation that published content meet high standards of factual accuracy and editorial oversight; failures of accuracy (e.g., fabricated citations) trigger investigation and potential retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference accuracy / no fabricated citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the citations at the end of chapters contained significant errors, referencing works or chapters of books that do not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References must point to real, verifiable works; fabricated or non-existent citations are a substantive integrity failure. The article confirmed some errors with people cited in the references as concrete examples of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: Using AI without declaration for anything besides copy editing is against Springer Nature’s policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors use generative AI for substantive content (not just copy editing), they must declare that use per publisher policy. Failure to declare AI use is a policy violation and raises concerns about content provenance and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize AI-specific failure modes (e.g., fabricated content/citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: These types of errors are common in text generated by large language models like ChatGPT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors, reviewers, and readers should be alert to characteristic LLM errors (hallucinated facts, fabricated references). Reliance on LLMs for substantive content without verification is an anti-pattern and can produce essentially useless or misleading work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction process must include a retraction note (transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper retraction requires a retraction note from the publisher related to the original publication; simply erasing information is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions should be documented with an explicit notice explaining the reason for retraction and linked to the original record; removing the item without a clear retraction statement can be perceived as a cover-up and impedes the record of scholarly correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction labeling and post-retraction availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The book 'is being retypeset, including with the addition of a retraction note, to reflect its retracted status. Once that has been completed, it will be back on the website (clearly marked as retracted).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reinstating a retracted work on the publisher site, the record must be clearly marked as retracted (retraction note visible) so users can see the corrected status and the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher investigation and root-cause analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher is 'reviewing this case carefully so we can understand what went wrong and ensure it does not happen again.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When integrity failures occur, publishers should investigate editorial and production workflows to identify systemic weaknesses and implement corrective measures to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim access controls (pause access) and library/publisher communication
rubrics_metrics.description: A reader asked her university library to 'pause access, or ask Springer Nature for an explanation or refund.' The library paused/removes the book from its catalog pending publisher response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Libraries and institutions may pause access or remove items from catalogs while awaiting publisher clarification. Publishers are expected to communicate with purchasers and library customers about the issue and remedy (including refunds where appropriate) as part of responsible post-publication handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of corrective editorial work (accuracy checking before re-publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters and the article suggest that 'retypesetting' alone may not solve substantive accuracy problems and that publishers should invest in 'accuracy checking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective action should include substantive fact-checking and verification of references and claims before reissuing material; cosmetic fixes without verification are an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent: publishers do retract books
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature has retracted books before, as have other publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction of book-length works is an established part of scholarly publishing practice; existence of precedent implies there are established processes and expectations (notice, documentation, communication) that should be followed.
